events.title: Establishment of Bac Lieu Province
events.description: Governor-General of French Indochina Paul Doumer signed a Decree separating the Bac Lieu arrondissement from Ha Tien Province to establish Bac Lieu Province. The province officially began operations on January 1, 1900. This marked the beginning of the provincial-level administrative unit of this land.

events.title: Creation of the song 'Da co hoai lang'
events.description: In Vinh Huong Village, musician Cao Van Lau composed the song 'Da co hoai lang' (Hearing the Night Drumbeats and Yearning for My Husband). This work is the predecessor of 'vong co' songs, marking a brilliant development of Don ca tai tu art and Southern Cai luong theater.

events.title: Ninh Thanh Loi Uprising
events.description: Ninh Thanh Loi peasants, under the leadership of 'Chu Chot' (Tran Kim Tuc), rose up to fight against the land grabbing by French landlords and their henchmen. Although bloodily suppressed, this event demonstrated the strong spirit of resistance of Bac Lieu peasants before the establishment of the Communist Party.

events.title: Dong Noc Nan Incident
events.description: The peasant family of Bien Toai and Muoi Chuc in Noc Nan field (Phong Thanh) bravely fought against tyrants, landlords, and colonial police who came to steal their rice and land. The case shocked all of Indochina, forcing the colonial court to acquit the victim's family.

events.title: Establishment of the First Party Cell (Phong Thanh Village)
events.description: Immediately after the Communist Party of Vietnam was founded, the first Party Cell of Bac Lieu Province was established in Phong Thanh Village (now in Gia Rai), with Comrade Nguyen Van Uye (Chin Uye) as Secretary. This was the first revolutionary leadership core of the province.

events.title: Seizing Power in Bac Lieu (A Bloodless Victory)
events.description: Under the ingenious leadership of the Provisional Provincial Party Committee and the Viet Minh Front, the masses surrounded the Governor's Palace. With cleverness and prestige, we persuaded Governor Truong Cong Thien to surrender, seizing full power without firing a single bullet.

events.title: Dong Khoi Movement in Bac Lieu (Chau Thanh - Vinh Loi)
events.description: Responding to the Ben Tre Dong Khoi movement, the Bac Lieu Provincial Party Committee mobilized the masses to rise up in Chau Thanh and Vinh Loi districts... breaking the enemy's grip, dismantling outposts, expanding the liberated zone, and defeating the enemy's national policy of 'Strategic Hamlets'.

events.title: Tet Mau Than Offensive in Bac Lieu
events.description: The provincial armed forces attacked Bac Lieu town, capturing the Administrative Building, the Police Department, and enemy barracks. The fighting raged fiercely right inside the inner city; we controlled the situation for many hours and inflicted heavy losses on the enemy.

events.title: Liberation of Bac Lieu Province
events.description: On the morning of April 30, our troops entered the town. Under military pressure and enemy proselytizing, the Governor of Bac Lieu, Colonel Nguyen Ngoc Diep, declared unconditional surrender at 10:30 AM. Bac Lieu was liberated early and completely, preserving its infrastructure.

events.title: Re-establishment of Bac Lieu Province
events.description: The 9th National Assembly passed a Resolution to split Minh Hai Province (which had been merged since 1976) into two provinces: Bac Lieu and Ca Mau. Bac Lieu Province officially began operations on January 1, 1997, starting its journey of economic recovery and development.

events.title: Groundbreaking of Bac Lieu Wind Power Plant
events.description: The first large-scale offshore wind power project in Vietnam commenced construction in the coastal area of Bac Lieu. This wind farm not only provides clean energy but has also become a new tourism symbol of the province.
